title: A regular asks whether Angie is there; she knows the voice, the grandchild and what was said last time
purpose: Story S5. Why customers ask for her. A regular whose car was slow to start remembers that Angie said something about the battery. Angie has the note, asks what the car has done, gives the price with what could change it and two times, books and sums up. Every check that applies is at its top level.

call.day: the Monday of week T-3 (rule R6; card S05, call 27)

scenario.who_calls: A regular of the Bonny Oaks shop, Carolyn Bivens, who has dealt with Angie for years.
scenario.job: battery, installed, after a test of the charging system
scenario.wants: to talk to Angie about a car that was slow to start
scenario.what_happens: Angie knows her voice, asks after her grandson, finds the note from the last visit (the battery tested weak), asks what the car has done since, gives the installed price and what would change the job, offers two times, books tomorrow at 7:30 and sums up with the address.

facts.note: catalogue.json battery_replace, class suv, standard: 272.20 (a menu price; the battery scales with the class). The customer does not ask what it costs, so the price check does not apply.

script.said: Brennan Auto Care on Bonny Oaks, this is Angie.
Oh, good. I was — I was gonna ask if Angie was there.
You found her. Is this Miss Carolyn?
It is. How'd you know?
I'd know your voice anywhere. How are you? How's that grandbaby?
Oh, he's walkin' now. Into everything.
I bet he is. What's going on with the Enclave?
Well, it didn't want to start this mornin'. It — it did, but it thought about it. And I remembered you told me somethin' about the battery last time.
I did. Let me pull you up... Yes ma'am. When you were in for your oil change, the battery tested weak. It still passed, but I wrote you a note that it was on borrowed time.
Uh-huh.
Well, you were right.
I'd rather have been wrong. Has it done it more than the once? Any clicking, or the lights dimming?
Just slow. Twice last week, and then this mornin'.

Okay. Then I don't want you getting stranded at the grocery store. The battery for your Enclave is two seventy-two installed. We'll test the charging system first, because if the alternator isn't keeping it up, a new battery won't fix that, and I'd call you before we went any further. I can take you tomorrow morning at seven-thirty, or Wednesday at two.
Okay.
Tomorrow. I don't trust it.
Tomorrow at seven-thirty. I've got you down, and I'll be right here at the counter. Are you going to wait, or do you want Josh to run you home?
I'll wait. I'll bring my book.

Good. It's about thirty minutes once it's in the bay. So that's tomorrow at seven-thirty, here at sixty-three-forty Bonny Oaks, and we're testing the charging system and putting a battery in the Enclave.
Okay.
Thank you, honey. I knew you'd know.
You're welcome, Miss Carolyn. Park right by the door, in case it's slow in the morning.
I will. Bye-bye.
